name: ADT plus an Androgen-Receptor Pathway Inhibitor (mCSPC)

biomarkers.note: ADT plus an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) is a category 1 treatment intensification for metastatic castration-sensitive disease; it is not biomarker-restricted. ADT is the required castration backbone. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Prostate Cancer, PROS-G (ADT for mCSPC) and Discussion.

lineOfTherapy: first-line systemic treatment intensification for metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (ADT plus an ARPI: abiraterone, apalutamide, enzalutamide, or darolutamide); may be combined with docetaxel as triplet therapy in fit patients

eligibilityCriteria.locator: v6.2026, PROS-G (ADT for Patients with mCSPC), prostate lines 2951 to 2961

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: concurrent ADT to maintain castrate testosterone below 50 ng/dL (orchiectomy, LHRH agonist, or LHRH antagonist)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v6.2026, PROS-G footnote h, prostate line ~2999

drugs.name: Abiraterone acetate
drugs.route: PO (once daily after an overnight fast)

provenance.locator: PROS-G footnote b, prostate lines 2846 to 2849 (standard formulation 1000 mg/day after an overnight fast; concurrent prednisone 5 mg PO once daily in the CSPC setting without docetaxel, or twice daily in the CSPC setting with docetaxel)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate v6.2026, PROS-G footnote b (prostate lines 2846 to 2849). Standard abiraterone acetate 1000 mg PO once daily on an empty stomach (after an overnight fast). MUST be given with concurrent prednisone (see prednisone entry). Fine-particle formulation and a low-fat 250 mg/day option exist per the same footnote; those are alternatives and not modeled here.

drugs.name: Prednisone (with abiraterone)

provenance.locator: PROS-G footnote b, prostate line 2847 (prednisone 5 mg PO once daily in the CSPC setting without docetaxel, or twice daily in the CSPC setting with docetaxel)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate v6.2026, PROS-G footnote b (prostate line 2847). Prednisone 5 mg PO ONCE daily when abiraterone is given as an ADT doublet (CSPC without docetaxel); 5 mg PO TWICE daily when given as triplet therapy with docetaxel. Mandatory companion steroid for the standard abiraterone formulation (with the fine-particle formulation, methylprednisolone 4 mg PO twice daily is used instead).

drugs.name: Apalutamide

provenance.locator: Discussion, prostate lines 6835 and 7345 (apalutamide 240 mg/day with ADT, TITAN)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate v6.2026 Discussion (prostate lines 6835, 7345). Apalutamide 240 mg PO once daily continuously. No companion steroid required. Alternative ARPI option (choose one ARPI).

drugs.name: Enzalutamide

provenance.locator: Discussion, prostate lines 6880 and 6467 (enzalutamide 160 mg/day plus ADT; ARCHES/ENZAMET-era evidence)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate v6.2026 Discussion (prostate lines 6880, 6467). Enzalutamide 160 mg PO once daily continuously. No companion steroid required. Alternative ARPI option (choose one ARPI).

drugs.name: Darolutamide

provenance.locator: Discussion, prostate line 7368 (darolutamide 600 mg twice daily); prostate line 6901 (ARANOTE darolutamide with ADT)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate v6.2026 Discussion (prostate line 7368). Darolutamide 600 mg PO TWICE daily (two 300 mg tablets twice daily) continuously, with food. No companion steroid required. In mCSPC, darolutamide is category 1 as triplet therapy with docetaxel (ARASENS) and studied as an ADT doublet (ARANOTE, prostate line 6901). Alternative ARPI option (choose one ARPI).

supportiveCare: SELECT ONE ARPI (abiraterone with prednisone, apalutamide, enzalutamide, or darolutamide); the four are modeled as alternatives, not given together.
continue ADT (LHRH agonist/antagonist or orchiectomy) throughout to maintain castrate testosterone below 50 ng/dL (PROS-G footnote h).
cycles null: continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
abiraterone requires mandatory concurrent prednisone (5 mg once daily as a doublet, twice daily if given with docetaxel as triplet).

monitoring: PSA and serum testosterone (confirm castrate level)
abiraterone: liver function, blood pressure, potassium, and fluid retention (mineralocorticoid excess)
enzalutamide/apalutamide: seizure risk, falls, fatigue; apalutamide: rash, thyroid function

doseModificationRules.text: Hold abiraterone and prednisone per labeling for grade 3 or higher hepatotoxicity; resume at a reduced dose after recovery; obtain clinical review.
Hold and dose-reduce the selected ARPI per labeling; obtain clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors (abiraterone, apalutamide, enzalutamide, darolutamide) added to ADT improve survival in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer

guideline.locator: PROS-G (ADT for mCSPC with treatment intensification), prostate lines 2951 to 2961; PROS-G footnote b (abiraterone 1000 mg/day + prednisone), prostate lines 2846 to 2849; Discussion doses: apalutamide 240 mg/day (prostate lines 6835, 7345), enzalutamide 160 mg/day (prostate lines 6880, 6467), darolutamide 600 mg twice daily (prostate line 7368)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for ADT plus an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (disease #53 mCSPC). Four interchangeable ARPI options are modeled, each dose-grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate v6.2026: abiraterone acetate 1000 mg PO once daily after an overnight fast plus prednisone 5 mg PO once daily as a doublet (twice daily if given with docetaxel as triplet) per PROS-G footnote b (prostate lines 2846 to 2849); apalutamide 240 mg PO daily (Discussion prostate lines 6835, 7345); enzalutamide 160 mg PO daily (Discussion prostate lines 6880, 6467); darolutamide 600 mg PO twice daily (Discussion prostate line 7368). ADT is the required castration backbone (PROS-G footnote h). Select one ARPI; the agents are alternatives, not combined. cycleLengthDays 28 with cycles null (continuous oral daily dosing until progression). No dose was invented or inferred. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
